%n ītanhā | birkāšu | enkīdu || ša ill[aku | būlšu]

manuscripts.atf:
i#-ta-an-ha bi-ir-ka-šu {d}en-ki-du₁₀ ša i#-l[a-ku bu-ul-šu]
$ single ruling

lines.translation: #tr.en: Enkidu’s legs grew weary, whose [herd was] on [the move];

variants.reconstruction:
%n [īš]u | uznam | enkīdu || watar | hasīsam
// L I.4 SB "I" 200

manuscripts.atf:
[i-š]u uz₄-na-am {d}en-ki-du₁₀ wa-tar ha-si₂-sa₃-am
$ line continues

lines.translation: #tr.en: Enkidu [had] reason, excelling in understanding.

manuscripts.atf:
uk-ta#-m[i-is-ma it-ta-ša-ab] | ma-ha-ar ha#-ri#-[im-tim]
$ single ruling

lines.translation: #tr.en: He squatted [him down and sat] before the [harlot,]

manuscripts.atf:
u₃?# i-na la# ša#-a-ti#
$ line continues

lines.translation: #tr.en: and in a manner not (formerly) his,

variants.reconstruction:
%n ša harimtum | ītawwû || išemmê | uznā[šu]
// L I.4 SB "I" 203

manuscripts.atf:
ša# ha#-ri-im#-tum i-ta-wu-u₂ i-še-me-e ez-na-[šu]
$ single ruling

lines.translation: #tr.en: [his] ears began hearing the harlot’s talk:

variants.reconstruction:
%n [har]imtum | ana šâšim | issaqqara(m) | ana enkī[du]
// L I.4 SB "I" 204

manuscripts.atf:
[ha-r]i-im-tum a-na ša#-ši-im# i-sa₃-qar-ra a-na {d}en-ki-[du₁₀]
$ single ruling

lines.translation: #tr.en: [the] harlot said to him, to Enkidu:

manuscripts.atf:
[al-k]a-am lu-ur#-di#-ka# {d}en-ki#-du₁₀ a-na li-bi uruk{ki} ri-bi-tim
$ line continues

lines.translation: #tr.en: “Come, let me lead you, Enkidu, into Uruk-the-City,

manuscripts.atf:
a-na bi-[tim el-li-im mu-ša-bi-(im) ša a-nim]
$ single ruling

lines.translation: #tr.en: to the [holy house, the dwelling of Anum!]

manuscripts.atf:
[ti-be₂ lu-ru-k]a {d#}en-ki-du₁₀ a-na li-bi UNUG{ki} ri-bi-tim
$ line continues

lines.translation: #tr.en: [Arise, let me take] you, Enkidu, into Uruk-the-City,

manuscripts.atf:
a-na E₂.AN.NA el-li#-[im mu-ša-bi-(im) ša iš₈-tar₂]
$ line continues

lines.translation: #tr.en: to the holy Eanna, [the dwelling of Ištar,]

variants.reconstruction:
%n [ašar | gilgāmeš || g]itmāla | emūqam
// L I.4 SB "I" 209

manuscripts.atf:
[a-šar {d}GIŠ] gi#-it#-ma#-la# e-mu-qa₂-am
$ line continues

lines.translation: #tr.en: [where Gilgameš,] superb of strength,

variants.reconstruction:
%n kīma rīmi | īteddiqu | [qarnī?]
// L I.4 SB "I" 210

manuscripts.atf:
ki-ma AM-MEŠ i-te-di#-qu₂-u₂# [qa₂-ar-ni?]
$ single ruling

lines.translation: #tr.en: like a wild bull wears [@i{a pair of horns}.]”

variants.reconstruction:
%n [ītawwâššum-ma | magir | qa]bâša
// L I.4 SB "I" 211

manuscripts.atf:
[i-ta-wa-aš-šum-ma ma-gi-ir qa₂]-ba#-ša#
$ line continues

lines.translation: #tr.en: [She talked to him and] what she [said found favour,]

variants.reconstruction:
%n libba | rabi | ina huršā[nī]
// cf. L I.4 SB "I" 212

manuscripts.atf: li-ba ra-bi i-na# hu-ur-ša-a#-[ni]

lines.translation: #tr.en: he was stoutest of “heart” in all the uplands.

variants.reconstruction:
%n [enkīdu | ana šâši]m || issaqqara(m) | ana har[imtim]
// L I.4 SB "I" 215

manuscripts.atf: [{d}en-ki-du₁₀ a-na ša-ši-i]m#! i#-sa₃#-qar#-ra# a#-na# ha#-ri#-[im-tim]

lines.translation: #tr.en: [Enkidu] said [to her,] to the harlot:

manuscripts.atf:
[{d}GIŠ lu-ka-a]l-li#-im#-k[a x (x x)] x x [x x x (x x)]
$ single ruling

variants.intertext: A long gap intervenes. When the text resumes the prostitute is talking to Enkidu

lines.translation: #tr.en: “[I will] show you [Gilgameš …]

variants.reconstruction: %n [... lul]likam

manuscripts.atf:
[x x x (x) lu-ul]-li-kam
$ line continues

lines.translation: #tr.en: [I will] come […]

variants.reconstruction:
%n tāwītka | lūmur | ... [...]
// L I.4 OB "II" 174

manuscripts.atf:
ta-wi-iš#-ka lu-mu-ur x x [x x x x (x x)]
$ single ruling

lines.translation: #tr.en: I would witness what you have talked about […]

variants.reconstruction:
%n [illak | in]a pānīšu || u šamkatum | ina wark[īšu]
// L I.4 OB "II" 175

manuscripts.atf:
[i-il-la-ak] i#-na# pa#-ni#-šu u₃ ša-am-ka-tum i-na# wa#-ar#-k[i-šu]
$ single ruling

lines.translation: #tr.en: [He going] in front and Šamkatum following behind [him,]

variants.reconstruction:
%n [īrub-ma | ana libbi (|) uruk | rib]ītim
// L I.4 OB "II" 177

manuscripts.atf:
[i-ru-ub-ma a-na li-bi UNUG{ki} ri-b]i-tim
$ line continues

lines.translation: #tr.en: [he went right into Uruk-the]-City.

variants.reconstruction:
%n enkīdu | īdišam | ina dannūtī[šu]
// cf. L I.4 SB "II" 101

manuscripts.atf:
{d}en-ki-du₁₀ i-di-ša-am i-na da-an#-nu#-ti-[šu]
$ single ruling

lines.translation: #tr.en: Enkidu, individually in [his] might,

variants.reconstruction:
%n [izzizam-ma | in]a sūqim
// L I.4 OB "II" 179

manuscripts.atf:
[iz-zi-za-am-ma i-n]a su₂-qi₂#-im
$ line continues

lines.translation: #tr.en: [stood there] in the street,

manuscripts.atf:
pa-ah-ra-ni-im ni-šu i-na ṣe-er#-ri-[šu]
$ single ruling

lines.translation: #tr.en: the people were gathered together around [him.]

manuscripts.atf:
[a-na-mi {d}GIŠ m]a-ši-il pa-da#-at-tam
$ line continues

lines.translation: #tr.en: “In build he is the equal [of Gilgameš,]

manuscripts.atf:
la#-na#-am ša-pi-il-ma e-[ṣe-em-tam pu-ku-ul]
$ single ruling

lines.translation: #tr.en: (but) shorter in stature and [sturdier] of [bone.]

manuscripts.atf:
[mi-in-de ša i-wa-al-du i-na š]a-di#-i-im
$ line continues

lines.translation: #tr.en: [Surely it is he who was born in the] upland,

variants.reconstruction:
%n šizbam | ša nammaštê-[m]a | ītenn[iq]
// L I.4 OB "II" 188-189

manuscripts.atf: ši-iz-ba-am ša na-ma-aš-te-[m]a i-te-n[i-iq]

lines.translation: #tr.en: animals’ milk is what he used to [suck.]”
